A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same constricting-CBF sampling framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison. The earlier pillow and latent-diffusion experiments are retained under different appendix and figure numbers.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original Lorenz simulations, constrained image generations and a 100-episode Push-T evaluation. Appendix B contains additional image-generation results, including unsuccessful latent-space constraint enforcement.

after.justification: The original empirical studies remain, supplemented by quantitative image-distribution measurements, schedule comparisons, nonconvex window-selection experiments and controller-cutoff tests.

M1.justification: The core constricting-tube and minimum-norm QP sampler remains. Section 5.3 changes the reported robot barrier from first differences of velocity actions to squared second differences of position waypoints. Appendix A.2 introduces LogSumExp smoothing and softmax reference selection for disjunctive constraints. Algorithm 1 also corrects its printed damping factor to 1−αΔt.

E1.justification: Lorenz trajectories, bedroom imagery, Stable Diffusion and Push-T remain covered. Appendix A.2 adds a distinct image-generation requirement: matching either of two reference windows within a nonconvex union of acceptable sets. The pillow and latent-diffusion experiments are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: v3 adds an explicitly evaluated vanilla/unguided image-model comparator in the schedule study and controller-cutoff comparison, absent from the corresponding v1 window experiment. The Zampini projection comparison and Push-T DP/DP-DDIM comparators remain. Newly discussed HardFlow and reward-guidance methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.2.3 introduces a quantitative image-evaluation protocol: 500 samples per schedule against 500 vanilla samples, masked FID/KID/Vendi measurements, and fixed-noise linearization-error measurements at 200 sampling steps. Appendix A.3 adds controlled cutoff-time tests. Push-T changes its action interpretation and smoothness criterion, making its revised violation counts incompatible with a same-setting performance comparison.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive tests of previously unsupported design choices: linear versus exponential/polynomial schedules, their linearization errors and distributional effects, and controller removal at four sampling times. Appendix A.2 additionally tests the nonconvex-set claim through disjunctive window selection. The earlier qualitative image and latent-space failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: New Table 1 reports KID uncertainty as ±0.19×10^-2, described as standard error. v3 also specifies varying seeds for the 500-image samples and fixed seeds/noise for selected analyses. v1 reports episode averages without comparable uncertainty or seed information. These additions do not establish increased repeated training runs.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports schedule-dependent maximum linearization errors of 7.42, 10.04, 5.81 and 22.69, masked FID of 47.09–47.22, and Vendi scores of 6.62–6.66 versus vanilla's 7.35. New figures report nonconvex selection and cutoff outcomes. Under the revised Push-T smoothness definition, DP/DP-DDIM violations change from 12/16 to 14/19; guided violations remain zero, rewards remain unchanged, and guided inference time changes from 62.92 to 62.91 ms.

T1.justification: v1's stochastic continuous-time invariance theorem and Girsanov-based terminal-KL equality, including their appendix proofs, are replaced by deterministic Proposition 4.1, exact discrete-time invariance under αΔt≤1, and a discrete KL upper-bound theorem with a new derivation. Section 4.3 distinguishes stochastic O(Δt) from deterministic O(Δt²) linearization remainders. Appendix A.2 adds formal disjunctive-set and smoothed-barrier definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions substantially redefine the central guarantees: v3 explicitly claims exact discrete-time safety for every realized noise sequence, while continuous-time formal safety is restricted to deterministic dynamics. Contribution 1 drops the boundedness restriction on the closed safe set. Contribution 2 now describes minimizing a per-step contribution to a KL bound. The training-free modularity claim remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of schedule-dependent numerical stability, attributes approximately 10% diversity reduction to the shared window constraint, and recommends stronger exponential constriction. The cutoff analysis explains how later control preserves finer detail, while the nonconvex study qualifies success by reference compatibility with the learned prior. Existing semantic-classifier and latent-decoder limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents schedule parameters, masking procedures, seed controls, cutoff values and softmax target construction for its additional studies. Image-QP timings are newly reported, although Table 1 calls them per-step and the discussion calls them per-sample. The solver stack, hardware and anonymized implementation-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises positioning by adding inference-time alignment literature and an explicit comparison with HardFlow, while removing the standalone strict-projection discussion and several associated references. It also newly attributes the constricting-tube concept to Gadginmath et al. (2026), presenting Proposition 4.1 as an adaptation of that work. This changes the stated intellectual foundation, beyond adding citations.

P1.justification: The central exposition is extensively reorganized around deterministic motivation, discrete-time guarantees and a separate linearized implementation section. Discretization moves into the preliminaries, and replacement proofs appear in the main text instead of the former proof appendix. Related-work paragraphs are revised, the experimental appendix is reorganized, and a Broader Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: v3 adds a quantitative schedule table and distinct visual comparisons for schedules, disjunctive constraints and controller cutoff. Earlier figures are retained, with several resized, relocated or relabeled; the Push-T table receives a shorter caption above the table. Wider text areas and changed spacing substantially reflow the document and its displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly qualitative image evidence, v3 provides useful quantitative scrutiny and targeted schedule, cutoff and nonconvex tests. It also clarifies the exact-condition versus linearized-implementation distinction and corrects the stated stochastic remainder order. The net gain is limited: the implemented QP still lacks the advertised exact safety guarantee, and Theorem 4.3 treats transitions conditioned on the realized noise as Gaussian, leaving the central distribution-shift justification unsupported.
